newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BELGIAN BROKERS PUT DELHAIZE 1996 EPS AT 90 BFR.
newsitem.headline: BELGIAN BROKERS PUT DELHAIZE 1996 EPS AT 90 BFR.

text.p: Earnings at Belgian retailer Delhaize "Le Lion", which last week posted a 22 percent rise in first-half 1996 group net profit, will be hit by a lower U.S. dollar and poorer performances by two foreign subsidiaries, Belgian broker Bank Degroof said.

"We revise our long-term earnings scenario downwards to reflect a less bullish view on the dollar and a less positive outlook for Super Discount Markets in U.S. and PG Group in France," said Degroof analyst Jan Longeval in a research note.
Longeval revised forecast 1996 earnings per share to 90 Belgian francs from 94, saying it was unlikely the second half would show better year-on-year growth than the first half.
"Our dividend discount model points to overvaluation, but as the stock continues to bask in an ongoing series of good news, we rate it a 'hold'," he said.
Broker Bank Paribas Belgium maintained its 'long-term buy' recommendation.

"For the whole year all foreign businesses should continue to contribute positively to Delhaize earnings. We maintain our 1996 earnings forecast of 90 francs per share," said Paribas analyst Benedicte Maron in a research note.
